---
title: "01 — BRFSS data audit and annual mental-distress prevalence"
subtitle: "2014–2024 | Survey-weighted descriptive analysis"
---

## Purpose and research context

This notebook establishes the descriptive context for the FMD project **before** model training. It measures annual coverage, outcome and predictor nonresponse, the distribution of BRFSS survey weights, and reported **frequent mental distress (FMD)** among American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN)-alone adults and other identified single-race adults.

**Outcome:** 
`FMD = 1` is defined as 14 or more self-reported mentally unhealthy days during the preceding 30 days; `FMD = 0` means fewer than 14 days. 

Unknown or refused outcomes are excluded from the prevalence numerator and denominator, but retained in the audit.

**Outputs:**
Two visible charts—annual prevalence with 95% confidence intervals and the annual AI/AN-minus-comparison difference with 95% confidence intervals—plus their supporting tables. 

`RAW_WEIGHT` is the unchanged CDC `_LLCPWT` weight, `STRAT` is `_STSTR`, and `PSU` corresponds to `_PSU` from BRFSS dataset. 

## 1. Load existing project helpers and attach the run

This cell finds the RStudio project and loads helpers and graph-palette modules. 

When called from the master notebook, it **uses the current run increment**; when knitted independently, it **allocates a new increment** so no previous artifacts are overwritten.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
# Find the existing RStudio project root
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)

    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }

        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio before running this notebook.")
        }

        current <- parent
    }
}

project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

# Evaluate the shared modules are in the environment 
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(lines, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(lines) == "```")

    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing executable chunk or closing fence in ", path)
        }

        paste(lines[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })

    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}

load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

check_packages(c("data.table", "ggplot2", "scales", "survey"))

# Keep the master-notebook increment; but allocate a new one for standalone knitting.
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("ATG_RUN_ID", unset = ""))) {
    start_new_run()
}

run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Audit increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```

## 2. Load the historical dataset and audit respondent coverage

Measures how many respondents are available each year, how many have a usable mental-health outcome, whether their original annual weights are positive and finite, and how many states are represented. The audit takes place **before** excluding records with unknown FMD or race.

```{r yearly-coverage}
# Read the pooled 2014–2024 dataset 
historical <- read_historical()
historical[, cohort := race_group(AIAN_ALONE)]

# Tabulate survey availability by year.
annual_audit <- historical[
    ,
    .(
        respondents = .N,
        valid_fmd = sum(valid_outcome(FMD)),
        missing_fmd = sum(!valid_outcome(FMD)),
        valid_weights = sum(valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT)),
        invalid_weights = sum(!valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT)),
        reporting_states = data.table::uniqueN(STATE)
    ),
    by = YEAR
][order(YEAR)]

annual_audit[
    ,
    missing_fmd_pct := 100 * missing_fmd / respondents
]

save_table(annual_audit, "01_yearly_audit")
print(annual_audit)
```

## 3. Audit missing responses by year and population

Checks whether unknown outcomes and selected missing predictors are distributed similarly across study populations. 
```{r response-missingness}
# Recognize both true NA and the explicit Missing level used in this project.
is_missing_response <- function(values) {
    missing <- is.na(values)
    labels <- as.character(values)
    missing | (!missing & labels %in% c("", "Missing"))
}

# Count missing outcomes and selected predictor responses by year and cohort.
missingness <- historical[
    ,
    .(
        respondents = .N,
        missing_fmd = sum(!valid_outcome(FMD)),
        missing_income = sum(is_missing_response(INCOME_BAND)),
        missing_general_health = sum(is_missing_response(GENHLTH_CLEAN)),
        missing_physical_days = sum(is_missing_response(PHYSHLTH_DAYS))
    ),
    by = .(YEAR, cohort)
][order(YEAR, cohort)]

missingness[
    ,
    missing_fmd_pct := 100 * missing_fmd / respondents
]

save_table(missingness, "01_missingness_by_year_and_group")
print(missingness)
```

## 4. Examine annual survey-weight distributions

This measures how unequally the original **annual** weights are distributed. 

Audit annual survey weights: per-year respondent count, weight range, and
Kish effective sample size, (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2), which shrinks as weights
become more unequal. Weights only; ignores strata/PSU design effects.

```{r annual-weights}
# Summarize respondent weights 
weight_audit <- historical[
    valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT),
    .(
        respondents = .N,
        min_weight = min(RAW_WEIGHT),
        median_weight = median(RAW_WEIGHT),
        mean_weight = mean(RAW_WEIGHT),
        max_weight = max(RAW_WEIGHT),
        effective_n = sum(RAW_WEIGHT)^2 / sum(RAW_WEIGHT^2)
    ),
    by = YEAR
][order(YEAR)]

weight_audit[
    ,
    # Modifies the table in place
    effective_n_pct := 100 * effective_n / respondents
]

save_table(weight_audit, "01_annual_weight_audit")
print(weight_audit)
```

## 5. Compare weight-only effective sample sizes across populations

Uses respondents with a valid FMD outcome to show how much weight inequality reduces 
the information available within each comparison group. It helps explain why AI/AN 
annual intervals may be wider despite thousands of survey responses.

Weight audit by year and population (outcome-valid respondents only), to show
how unequal weights reduce the information available within each group.

```{r group-weights}
# Keep outcome-valid respondents in the two specified populations.
valid_groups <- historical[
    valid_outcome(FMD) &
        valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT) &
        cohort %in% primary_groups
]

# Retain the counts required for prevalence-table interpretation.
group_weight_audit <- valid_groups[
    ,
    .(
        n = .N,
        median_weight = median(RAW_WEIGHT),
        max_weight = max(RAW_WEIGHT),
        effective_n = sum(RAW_WEIGHT)^2 / sum(RAW_WEIGHT^2)
    ),
    by = .(YEAR, cohort)
][order(YEAR, cohort)]

group_weight_audit[
    ,
    effective_n_pct := 100 * effective_n / n
]

save_table(group_weight_audit, "01_group_weight_audit")
print(group_weight_audit)
```

## 6. Verify the structure of the survey-design identifiers

# Per-year STRAT/PSU audit; stops on repeated pairs or missing identifiers.

```{r survey-identifier-audit}
# Count sampling identifiers within each survey year.
design_audit <- historical[
    ,
    {
        unique_pairs <- data.table::uniqueN(.SD, by = c("STRAT", "PSU"))

        .(
            respondents = .N,
            unique_strata = data.table::uniqueN(STRAT),
            unique_psu_values = data.table::uniqueN(PSU),
            unique_stratum_psu_pairs = unique_pairs,
            duplicated_stratum_psu_pairs = .N - unique_pairs,
            missing_strata = sum(is.na(STRAT)),
            missing_psus = sum(is.na(PSU))
        )
    },
    by = YEAR,
    .SDcols = c("STRAT", "PSU")
][order(YEAR)]

save_table(design_audit, "01_survey_identifier_audit")
print(design_audit)

# Halt if any year violates the one-record-per-pair assumption.
if (any(design_audit$duplicated_stratum_psu_pairs > 0)) {
    stop("Repeated stratum-PSU pairs found: verify the design before computing CIs.")
}

if (any(design_audit$missing_strata > 0 | design_audit$missing_psus > 0)) {
    stop("Missing design identifiers found: resolve before computing CIs.")
}
```

## 7. Detail the design diagnostic

Annual survey-design audit (2014-2024): respondents, strata, distinct PSU
values, stratum-PSU pairs, multi-respondent units, singleton strata, and
missing identifiers. 

```{r design-2024-details}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Audit BRFSS survey design across all years (2014–2024)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Examine the number of respondents assigned to each
# stratum/PSU combination within each survey year.
#
# YEAR must be included because survey identifiers may
# be reused across different annual BRFSS datasets.

psu_pairs <- historical[
    ,
    .(respondents_per_psu = .N),
    by = .(YEAR, STRAT, PSU)
]

# Count distinct PSUs within each sampling stratum
# for each survey year.

strata_summary <- psu_pairs[
    ,
    .(psus_in_stratum = .N),
    by = .(YEAR, STRAT)
]

# Summarize the number of unique PSU values within each year.
# These counts are not necessarily the number of survey units
# because PSU identifiers may repeat between strata.

psu_counts <- historical[
    ,
    .(
        respondents = .N,
        distinct_psu_values = data.table::uniqueN(PSU),
        missing_strata = sum(is.na(STRAT)),
        missing_psus = sum(is.na(PSU))
    ),
    by = YEAR
]

# Calculate the actual number of distinct stratum/PSU pairs,
# as well as the number containing multiple respondents.

psu_structure <- psu_pairs[
    ,
    .(
        distinct_stratum_psu_pairs = .N,
        multi_respondent_units = sum(respondents_per_psu > 1)
    ),
    by = YEAR
]

# Identify sampling strata containing only one PSU.

singleton_summary <- strata_summary[
    ,
    .(
        total_strata = .N,
        singleton_strata = sum(psus_in_stratum == 1)
    ),
    by = YEAR
]

# Combine the diagnostics into one annual audit table.

design_summary <- merge(
    psu_counts,
    psu_structure,
    by = "YEAR"
)

design_summary <- merge(
    design_summary,
    singleton_summary,
    by = "YEAR"
)

# Sort by survey year and arrange columns for readability.

data.table::setcolorder(
    design_summary,
    c(
        "YEAR",
        "respondents",
        "total_strata",
        "distinct_psu_values",
        "distinct_stratum_psu_pairs",
        "multi_respondent_units",
        "singleton_strata",
        "missing_strata",
        "missing_psus"
    )
)

data.table::setorder(design_summary, YEAR)

# Save the results using the existing run-increment system.

save_table(
    design_summary,
    "01_survey_design_annual"
)

# Display the survey-design audit in the notebook.

print(design_summary)
```

## 8. Estimate annual FMD prevalence and its 95% confidence intervals

This is the **main descriptive analysis**. For each year from 2014 to 2024, the code first constructs a stratified survey design using **all records with usable annual weights**. 

After constructing the design, it subsets to the two populations. Unknown mental-health outcomes are kept as `NA` and excluded by `na.rm = TRUE` when estimating prevalence.

Annual point estimates use the year-specific `RAW_WEIGHT`. Standard errors and intervals account for the specified stratification and weights. The lonely-PSU adjustment is an approximation; results depend on correct original CDC variable mappings and preprocessing exclusions.

**Note: warning summary is included for clean read-out:** Some full-sample strata contain only one respondent, and some strata may contain only one eligible respondent within an analysis domain. The `survey` package can warn about each such stratum even when `survey.lonely.psu = "adjust"` is active. The notebook retains that variance adjustment but intercepts **only the exact singleton-PSU warning** and summarizes it by year for clarity. Other warnings remain visible. This makes the output easier to read without concealing the design limitation.

```{r survey-prevalence-by-year}
# Apply an explicit adjustment for strata or domains with one PSU.
options(
    survey.lonely.psu = "adjust",
    survey.adjust.domain.lonely = TRUE
)

# Work one year at a time to avoid constructing a giant pooled survey object.
prevalence_rows <- vector("list", length = 11L)
gap_rows <- vector("list", length = 11L)
singleton_warning_rows <- vector("list", length = 11L)
analysis_years <- 2014:2024

for (year_index in seq_along(analysis_years)) {
    year <- analysis_years[year_index]
    cat("[SURVEY] Estimating", year, "\n")

    # Keep all source records with valid annual weights for the design.
    data_year <- data.table::copy(
        historical[YEAR == year & valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT)]
    )

    # Preserve unknown FMD outcomes as missing, never as a negative response.
    data_year[
        ,
        fmd_value := ifelse(valid_outcome(FMD), as.numeric(FMD), NA_real_)
    ]

    # Count singleton strata before any subgroup or outcome filtering.
    # The count describes the retained processed annual dataset.
    stratum_sizes <- data_year[, .N, by = STRAT]
    singleton_strata <- sum(stratum_sizes$N == 1L)

    # Construct the full annual design before subgroup restriction.
    annual_design <- survey::svydesign(
        ids = ~1,
        strata = ~STRAT,
        weights = ~RAW_WEIGHT,
        data = as.data.frame(data_year)
    )

    group_design <- subset(
        annual_design,
        cohort %in% primary_groups
    )

    # Collect only the known singleton-PSU warnings during estimation.
    # Do not suppress unrelated warnings or survey-computation errors.
    warning_log <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    warning_log$lonely_psu <- character()

    # Estimate group prevalences and their joint covariance matrix.
    # The survey package still applies the configured adjustment.
    group_estimates <- withCallingHandlers(
        survey::svyby(
            ~fmd_value,
            ~cohort,
            design = group_design,
            FUN = survey::svymean,
            na.rm = TRUE,
            vartype = "se",
            covmat = TRUE
        ),
        warning = function(warning_condition) {
            warning_text <- conditionMessage(warning_condition)

            if (grepl(
                "has only one PSU at stage 1",
                warning_text,
                fixed = TRUE
            )) {
                warning_log$lonely_psu <- c(
                    warning_log$lonely_psu,
                    warning_text
                )

                # Muffle this already-documented warning only.
                invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
            }
        }
    )

    # Log the number of distinct design warnings and full-sample
    # singleton strata. A domain singleton can occur even when
    # the full stratum contains multiple respondents.
    singleton_warning_rows[[year_index]] <- data.table::data.table(
        YEAR = year,
        singleton_strata_full_sample = singleton_strata,
        singleton_warning_events = length(warning_log$lonely_psu),
        distinct_singleton_warnings = length(unique(warning_log$lonely_psu))
    )

    cat(
        "[DESIGN] ", year,
        ": ", singleton_strata, " singleton strata in the retained annual sample; ",
        length(unique(warning_log$lonely_psu)),
        " unique singleton warnings during subgroup estimation.\n",
        sep = ""
    )

    # Match the named cohorts; never assume the result's row ordering.
    observed_groups <- as.character(group_estimates$cohort)
    group_indices <- match(primary_groups, observed_groups)

    if (anyNA(group_indices)) {
        stop("Missing one of the two study groups in survey year ", year)
    }

    estimates <- as.numeric(stats::coef(group_estimates))[group_indices]
    covariance <- as.matrix(stats::vcov(group_estimates))[
        group_indices,
        group_indices,
        drop = FALSE
    ]

    standard_errors <- sqrt(diag(covariance))
    degrees_of_freedom <- survey::degf(group_design)
    critical_value <- stats::qt(0.975, df = degrees_of_freedom)

    # Group-specific annual prevalence and design-based confidence intervals.
    prevalence_rows[[year_index]] <- data.table::data.table(
        YEAR = year,
        cohort = primary_groups,
        observed_fmd = estimates,
        se = standard_errors,
        ci_l = estimates - critical_value * standard_errors,
        ci_u = estimates + critical_value * standard_errors,
        degrees_of_freedom = degrees_of_freedom
    )

    # Directly estimate the AI/AN minus comparison prevalence difference.
    contrast <- c(1, -1)
    difference <- sum(contrast * estimates)
    difference_se <- sqrt(
        as.numeric(t(contrast) %*% covariance %*% contrast)
    )

    gap_rows[[year_index]] <- data.table::data.table(
        YEAR = year,
        gap_pp = 100 * difference,
        se_pp = 100 * difference_se,
        ci_l_pp = 100 * (difference - critical_value * difference_se),
        ci_u_pp = 100 * (difference + critical_value * difference_se),
        degrees_of_freedom = degrees_of_freedom
    )

    # Release large design objects before processing the next survey year.
    rm(data_year, annual_design, group_design, group_estimates)
}

annual_prevalence <- data.table::rbindlist(prevalence_rows)
annual_gap <- data.table::rbindlist(gap_rows)
singleton_warning_audit <- data.table::rbindlist(singleton_warning_rows)

# Save the stratum diagnostics rather than printing warnings repeatedly.
save_table(singleton_warning_audit, "01_singleton_psu_warning_audit")
print(singleton_warning_audit)

# Join respondent counts and weight-only effective n to each group estimate.
annual_prevalence <- merge(
    annual_prevalence,
    group_weight_audit[, .(YEAR, cohort, n, effective_n, effective_n_pct)],
    by = c("YEAR", "cohort"),
    all.x = TRUE,
    sort = FALSE
)

data.table::setorder(annual_prevalence, YEAR, cohort)
data.table::setorder(annual_gap, YEAR)

# Store the exact values that appear in the two figures.
save_table(annual_prevalence, "01_annual_fmd_prevalence")
save_table(annual_gap, "01_annual_fmd_gap")

print(annual_prevalence)
print(annual_gap)
```

## 9. Figure 1 — Annual FMD prevalence with confidence intervals

**Measures** the estimated proportion reporting frequent mental distress in each year, separately for the two populations. The shaded ribbons are **95% design-based confidence intervals**.

```{r annual-prevalence-figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualize annual FMD prevalence, 2014–2024
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Measure:
# Display the annual survey-weighted proportion of adults
# reporting 14 or more mentally unhealthy days.
#
# The shaded ribbons represent 95% confidence intervals.
# The lines connect annual cross-sectional estimates;
# they do not represent changes within individuals.

# Verify that the plotted data contain valid estimates.
stopifnot(
    all(
        is.finite(annual_prevalence$observed_fmd) &
        is.finite(annual_prevalence$ci_l) &
        is.finite(annual_prevalence$ci_u)
    ),
    all(
        annual_prevalence$ci_l <=
            annual_prevalence$observed_fmd
    ),
    all(
        annual_prevalence$observed_fmd <=
            annual_prevalence$ci_u
    )
)

# Ensure the years and populations are in order.
data.table::setorder(
    annual_prevalence,
    cohort,
    YEAR
)

# Determine the plotting limit without removing any
# confidence interval values.
upper_limit <- max(
    annual_prevalence$ci_u,
    na.rm = TRUE
) * 1.08

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Construct the visualization
# ------------------------------------------------------------

prevalence_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    annual_prevalence,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = YEAR,
        y = observed_fmd,
        color = cohort,
        linetype = cohort,
        group = cohort
    )
) +
    # Mark 2020 as a temporal reference.
    # This marker does not imply a causal effect.
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
        xintercept = 2020,
        color = atg_palette[["gold"]],
        linetype = "dotted",
        linewidth = 0.6,
        alpha = 0.65
    ) +
    # Show the uncertainty around annual prevalence.
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
        ggplot2::aes(
            ymin = ci_l,
            ymax = ci_u,
            fill = cohort
        ),
        alpha = 0.16,
        color = NA,
        show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    # Connect annual estimates.
    ggplot2::geom_line(
        linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    # Mark each survey-year estimate.
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        size = 2.7
    ) +
    # Display every survey year.
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = 2014:2024
    ) +
    # Format prevalence as percentages.
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        breaks = seq(0, 0.30, by = 0.05),
        labels = scales::percent_format(
            accuracy = 1
        ),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(
            mult = c(0, 0.02)
        )
    ) +
    # Preserve a zero baseline.
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
        ylim = c(0, upper_limit)
    ) +
    # Apply the existing project palette.
    atg_scale_color_groups() +
    atg_scale_fill_groups() +
    # Distinguish groups without relying on color alone.
    ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual(
        name = "Population",
        values = c(
            "AI/AN alone" = "solid",
            "Other identified single-race" = "longdash"
        )
    ) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Frequent mental distress, 2014–2024",
        subtitle = paste(
            "Survey-weighted annual prevalence",
            "with 95% confidence intervals"
        ),
        x = "BRFSS survey year",
        y = "Adults reporting frequent mental distress",
        color = "Population",
        fill = "Population",
        linetype = "Population",
        caption = paste(
            "FMD = 14+ mentally unhealthy days",
            "in the past 30 days.",
            "Annual cross-sectional estimates;",
            "participating states vary by year.",
            "Intervals reflect the specified",
            "BRFSS survey design."
        )
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Display and save the visualization
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Display the graph directly in the R Notebook.
# Save a separate copy using the current run increment.

show_and_save(
    prevalence_plot,
    "01_annual_fmd_prevalence",
    11,
    6
)

```

## 10. Figure 2 — Annual AI/AN prevalence difference with confidence intervals

The percentage-point difference between AI/AN-alone and other single-race annual FMD prevalence.
Positive values mean higher estimated prevalence among AI/AN-alone adults.

```{r annual-gap-figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualize the annual FMD prevalence disparity
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Measure:
# Display the difference in survey-weighted frequent
# mental distress prevalence between AI/AN-alone adults
# and other identified single-race adults.
#
# Positive values indicate higher estimated FMD
# prevalence among AI/AN-alone respondents.
#
# Error bars show 95% confidence intervals calculated
# for the between-group difference within each year.
#
# This visualization does not test whether the
# disparity changed significantly between years.

# Validate the annual estimates and confidence intervals.

stopifnot(
    all(
        is.finite(annual_gap$gap_pp) &
        is.finite(annual_gap$ci_l_pp) &
        is.finite(annual_gap$ci_u_pp)
    ),
    all(annual_gap$ci_l_pp <= annual_gap$gap_pp),
    all(annual_gap$gap_pp <= annual_gap$ci_u_pp)
)

# Sort the observations chronologically.

data.table::setorder(annual_gap, YEAR)

# Leave additional room above the highest error bar.

upper_limit <- max(
    10,
    ceiling(max(annual_gap$ci_u_pp) + 0.5)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Construct the visualization
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gap_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    annual_gap,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = YEAR,
        y = gap_pp
    )
) +
    # Identify the beginning of the later study period.
    # This marker does not imply a causal effect.
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
        xintercept = 2020,
        linetype = "dotted",
        color = atg_palette[["gold"]],
        linewidth = 0.6,
        alpha = 0.65
    ) +
    # Mark zero as the absence of a prevalence difference.
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
        yintercept = 0,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = atg_palette[["gold"]],
        linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    # Show confidence intervals for the annual differences.
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
        ggplot2::aes(
            ymin = ci_l_pp,
            ymax = ci_u_pp
        ),
        width = 0.18,
        linewidth = 0.7,
        color = atg_palette[["turquoise"]]
    ) +
    # Connect the annual point estimates.
    ggplot2::geom_line(
        color = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
        linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    # Identify each annual estimate.
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        color = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
        size = 2.7
    ) +
    # Display every survey year.
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = 2014:2024
    ) +
    # Display the differences in percentage points.
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        breaks = seq(0, upper_limit, by = 2),
        labels = function(values) {
            paste0(values, " pp")
        }
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
        ylim = c(0, upper_limit)
    ) +
    # Apply the established project visual theme.
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = paste(
            "Disparity in frequent mental distress,",
            "2014–2024"
        ),
        subtitle = paste(
            "AI/AN alone minus other identified",
            "single-race adults"
        ),
        x = "BRFSS survey year",
        y = "Difference in FMD prevalence",
        caption = paste(
            "Points represent annual survey-weighted",
            "prevalence differences.",
            "Error bars show 95% confidence intervals",
            "for each annual difference.",
            "The zero line indicates no difference.",
            "State participation varies by year."
        )
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Display and save the visualization
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Display the graph directly inside the notebook.
# Save a copy using the current run increment.

show_and_save(
    gap_plot,
    "01_annual_fmd_gap",
    11,
    5.5
)

```

## 11. Figure 3 — Pre-2020 versus Post-2020 Disparity

### Research question

Did the difference in reported frequent mental distress
between AI/AN-alone adults and other identified single-race
adults increase after 2019?

### What this analysis measures

This analysis compares the average annual prevalence gap
across two periods:

- Pre-2020: 2014–2019 (6 years)
- Post-2020: 2020–2024 (5 years)

Each survey year contributes equally to its period average.

The analysis calculates:

1. Mean annual prevalence gap for each period.
2. Approximate 95% confidence intervals for both averages.
3. The post-2020 minus pre-2020 difference.
4. An approximate 95% confidence interval for that change.

The primary intervals combine annual survey-design standard
errors, assuming sampling independence between survey years.

A supplementary sensitivity analysis examines variation
between annual estimates.

These analyses are descriptive and do not establish that
the pandemic or another event caused a change in disparity.


```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Compare pre-2020 and post-2020 prevalence disparities
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Measure:
# Determine whether the average annual FMD prevalence
# gap differs between the two study periods.
#
# Each year contributes equally to its period average.
# Annual survey-design standard errors are propagated
# assuming independent annual survey samples.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Validate the existing annual gap estimates
# ------------------------------------------------------------

required_columns <- c("YEAR", "gap_pp", "se_pp")

stopifnot(
    all(required_columns %in% names(annual_gap)),
    !anyDuplicated(annual_gap$YEAR),
    all(2014:2024 %in% annual_gap$YEAR),
    all(is.finite(annual_gap$gap_pp)),
    all(is.finite(annual_gap$se_pp)),
    all(annual_gap$se_pp >= 0)
)

# Make a copy to preserve the original annual results.
period_data <- data.table::copy(annual_gap)

# Assign each survey year to its study period.
period_data[
    ,
    period := ifelse(
        YEAR < 2020,
        "2014–2019",
        "2020–2024"
    )
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate average annual disparities
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# The average gap is the arithmetic mean of yearly gaps.
#
# For independently sampled annual estimates, the
# variance of an equally weighted period mean is:
#
# sum(annual_variances) / number_of_years^2

period_summary <- period_data[
    ,
    .(
        years = .N,
        mean_gap_pp = mean(gap_pp),
        se_pp = sqrt(sum(se_pp^2)) / .N
    ),
    by = period
]

# Calculate approximate 95% confidence intervals.
# These reflect annual survey-sampling uncertainty,
# not uncertainty from year-to-year heterogeneity.

critical_value <- stats::qnorm(0.975)

period_summary[
    ,
    `:=`(
        ci_l_pp = mean_gap_pp - critical_value * se_pp,
        ci_u_pp = mean_gap_pp + critical_value * se_pp
    )
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate the change between periods
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pre <- period_summary[period == "2014–2019"]
post <- period_summary[period == "2020–2024"]

stopifnot(nrow(pre) == 1L, nrow(post) == 1L)

# Positive change indicates a larger prevalence
# disparity in the post-2020 period.

change_pp <- post$mean_gap_pp - pre$mean_gap_pp

# Propagate the uncertainty of the two period averages.
change_se <- sqrt(pre$se_pp^2 + post$se_pp^2)

# Calculate the approximate confidence interval.
change_ci_l <- change_pp - critical_value * change_se
change_ci_u <- change_pp + critical_value * change_se

# Calculate an approximate two-sided p-value.
change_z <- change_pp / change_se

change_p <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(change_z))

# Store the change as a separate result.
change_results <- data.table::data.table(
    comparison = "Post-2020 minus pre-2020",
    change_pp = change_pp,
    se_pp = change_se,
    ci_l_pp = change_ci_l,
    ci_u_pp = change_ci_u,
    p_value = change_p
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Examine year-to-year variation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# A supplementary Welch comparison treats the annual
# gap estimates as observations.
#
# This captures between-year variability but does not
# incorporate their individual survey-design variances.
# It is a sensitivity check, not a definitive alternative
# to a joint multiyear survey-design analysis.

year_sensitivity <- stats::t.test(
    period_data[period == "2020–2024", gap_pp],
    period_data[period == "2014–2019", gap_pp]
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Save and display results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

save_table(
    period_summary,
    "01_prepost_fmd_gap"
)

save_table(
    change_results,
    "01_prepost_fmd_gap_change"
)

cat("\nPRE/POST PREVALENCE GAP SUMMARY\n")
print(period_summary)

cat("\nCHANGE IN PREVALENCE GAP\n")
print(change_results)

cat("\nYEAR-TO-YEAR SENSITIVITY CHECK\n")
print(year_sensitivity)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Prepare Figure 3
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Combine the period averages with the estimated change.
# All three quantities are measured in percentage points,
# but the third row represents a difference of averages.

plot_data <- data.table::data.table(
    measure = c(
        "2014–2019 average gap",
        "2020–2024 average gap",
        "Change (post minus pre)"
    ),
    estimate_pp = c(
        pre$mean_gap_pp,
        post$mean_gap_pp,
        change_pp
    ),
    ci_l_pp = c(
        pre$ci_l_pp,
        post$ci_l_pp,
        change_ci_l
    ),
    ci_u_pp = c(
        pre$ci_u_pp,
        post$ci_u_pp,
        change_ci_u
    )
)

# Arrange rows from earliest period to the contrast.
plot_data[
    ,
    measure := factor(
        measure,
        levels = rev(measure)
    )
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Construct the visualization
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_data[
    ,
    label := sprintf(
        "%+.2f pp [%+.2f, %+.2f]",
        estimate_pp, ci_l_pp, ci_u_pp
    )
]

prepost_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = estimate_pp,
        y = measure,
        color = measure
    )
) +
    # Zero represents no prevalence gap or no change.
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
        xintercept = 0,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = atg_palette[["gold"]],
        linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    # Plot confidence intervals horizontally.
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
        ggplot2::aes(
            x = ci_l_pp,
            xend = ci_u_pp,
            yend = measure
        ),
        linewidth = 1.4
    ) +
    # Show the point estimates.
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        size = 3.8
    ) +
    # Label each estimate with its 95% CI; emphasize the change row.
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(
            label = label,
            fontface = ifelse(
                measure == "Change (post minus pre)", "bold", "plain"
            )
        ),
        vjust = -1.4,
        size = 3.6,
        show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    # Apply the project color palette.
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
        values = c(
            "2014–2019 average gap" = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
            "2020–2024 average gap" = atg_palette[["rust"]],
            "Change (post minus pre)" = atg_palette[["gold"]]
        )
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        labels = function(values) {
            paste0(round(values, 1), " pp")
        },
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(
            mult = c(0.08, 0.12)
        )
    ) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(
        legend.position = "none"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Average annual prevalence gap: 2014–2019 versus 2020–2024",
        subtitle = paste(
            "Average annual AI/AN minus comparison prevalence gap,",
            "before and after 2020"
        ),
        x = "Percentage points",
        y = NULL,
        caption = paste(
            "Points show equally weighted annual gap averages",
            "and their post-minus-pre difference.",
            "Intervals are approximate 95% survey-sampling CIs.",
            "Annual samples are assumed independent;",
            "changing state participation is not adjusted."
        )
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Show and save Figure 3
# ------------------------------------------------------------

show_and_save(
    prepost_plot,
    "01_prepost_fmd_gap_comparison",
    11,
    5.5
)

```
